recentItems.title: Why moms shouldn't have to do it all | Onnie Michalsky | TEDxBillings
recentItems.description:
This TEDx talk challenges the supermom myth and the unrealistic expectations placed on women in motherhood. It reveals the hidden costs of juggling the endless mental load, emotional labor, and invisible work that leave so many mothers burned out, anxious, and disconnected from themselves. Through powerful storytelling and research, it introduces a three-part antidote to Supermom Syndrome. Moms will walk away inspired to hang up the cape, reclaim their identity, and embrace self-care without guilt, while families, partners, and communities will discover why supporting mothers benefits everyone. 

Onnie Michalsky is a licensed therapist, consultant, and host of the Moms Without Capes Podcast. She’s passionate about helping women who feel lost under the weight of motherhood shed the do-it-all mindset, break through self-limiting beliefs, and make room for self-care and growth. As an advocate for mental health, Onnie has also joined forces with Upstream Strategy Partners to make mental health care more accessible in the workplace. Beyond her work, she leads a Faith-Driven Entrepreneur group, runs the Billings Mental Health Providers Alliance, and is an active Toastmasters member. Through therapy, advocacy, and community leadership, Onnie is dedicated to improving mental health, fostering personal growth, and helping individuals and organizations create lives and workplaces that are balanced, fulfilling, and mentally strong. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Where Democracy Lives: Leadership Before Confidence | Nadia Poluhina | TEDxMinneapolis
recentItems.description: Seeing her own name for local school board on the same ballot as candidates for president crystallized something Nadia Poluhina had only recently begun to understand: democracy happens much closer to home, and public service is not reserved for “other people.” It is a place where capable people can bring the skills and judgment they already have. Drawing on experience in finance, systems, and complex institutions, Nadia explores what happens when capable people assume public leadership belongs to someone else. When a school-district budget crisis made the stakes of local decision-making impossible to ignore, she realized that professional expertise could also become a form of civic stewardship. In this personal and humorous talk, Nadia argues that leadership is not about waiting until we feel completely ready. It is about recognizing what we can contribute, stepping into rooms where decisions are made, and accepting responsibility when our judgment is needed. Democracy is stronger when capable people stop assuming leadership belongs to someone else. Filmed August 4, 2026, at Orchestra Hall in Minneapolis. An immigrant, finance and healthcare leader, and newly elected school board member bringing a rare and powerful perspective on civic engagement to our stage. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Soft skills in the age of AI | Michael Streit | TEDxInnsbruck
recentItems.description: How often do you turn to AI when you have a question? And when the result disappoints you, what went wrong? There are times when involving AI is absolutely smart, but there are also times when it is even smarter to use human intelligence first. Michael is talking about what soft skills are required in the wavy times of AI and how his passion for surfing taught him enjoy the process. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: "I Can" Doesn't Mean "I Will" | Kai Chan | TEDxInnsbruck
recentItems.description: When was the last time you said yes to a commitment? And did your actions match your words? Saying yes is easy - acting on it is a choice. If you reflect honestly on that difference, your next yes will mean more. He is a student of the Technical University of Munich as well as Co-Founder, and Head of HR & Administration at Munich Music Labs. He will be talking about Honest Commitments. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The creative side of science | Verena Gautsch | TEDxInnsbruck
recentItems.description: What is the difference between art and neuroscience? For Verena, it is not the perspective you bring but the questions you are willing to ask, and the experiments that follow. That is creative problem solving, and the two fields have more in common than you might think. She is working as ob her PhD as Neuro- & Cancer Scientist at the University of Cambridge and tells us her insights about Creative Problem Solving. recentItems.title: The Power of Zero - Life is a Marathon, Not a Sprint | Syafiq Faruq | TEDxITECCYouth
recentItems.description:
In this talk, Syafiq shares his personal journey of overcoming academic setbacks and repeated rejections, highlighting how finding a pathway aligned with his passion for sports transformed his life. 

Despite initially struggling academically and facing multiple rejections from polytechnic, he persevered and went on to pursue a degree, a Master's and a doctoral programme in sports and exercise science. 

Drawing parallels with his experience as a marathon runner, he emphasises the importance of resilience, consistency and making small, incremental improvements. 

He also highlights the importance of leading by example in his role as a healthcare professional and advocating for healthier living. He is a firm believer of encouraging students to recognise that their starting point does not determine their destination, and that zero represents a fresh start and an opportunity for growth...not failure. Syafiq Faruq is an ITE alumnus and allied health professional who graduated with a Higher Nitec in Sport Management in 2018. With a background in sports science and clinical exercise physiology, he is also actively involved in youth mentoring and engagement.

His journey from ITE reflects resilience, self-belief and continuous growth, making his experiences particularly relatable to ITE students.

His story connects with The Power of Zero; demonstrating how one’s starting point need not define where one can go, and how the courage to take the first step can lead to meaningful growth and achievement. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Power of Zero - From Janitor to CEO  | Shane Chiang | TEDxITECCYouth
recentItems.description:
Watch and hear Shane Chiang as he shares his personal journey of overcoming academic struggles, financial hardships and career setbacks to illustrate the Power of Zero; the ability to start afresh and turn challenges into opportunities. 

From repeating Primary 2 and taking on menial jobs to becoming a Chief Marketing Officer at Nokia and subsequently founding his own cybersecurity company, he demonstrates that one's beginnings do not determine one's future. He emphasises the importance of perseverance, continuous learning and having the courage to embrace new beginnings. 

Through his experiences, he encourages us to view failures as opportunities for growth rather than reasons to give up. The message is simple; yet profound: No matter how many times you start from zero...you always have the power to rewrite your story. Shane Chiang is the Founder and CEO of Momentum Z, a cybersecurity, AI governance and digital trust consultancy advising organisations across Asia.

Currently pursuing a Doctorate in Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence and Sustainability, he advocates curiosity, adaptability and continuous learning in navigating technological change.

His journey reflects The Power of Zero; that progress can begin without certainty, through the willingness to start, learn and keep building. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Power of Zero - Starting from Zero in a Changing World  | Athan Leroy Lim | TEDxITECCYouth
recentItems.description:
ITE student Athan Leroy Lim shares his experience representing ITE at the ITE-VTC International Student Seminar 2026, reflecting on the uncertainties and challenges of stepping into an unfamiliar environment. 

Through interactions with students from Hong Kong and Shenzhen, he discovered the value of cross-cultural connections, collaboration and embracing different perspectives. His involvement in the seminar's social media team also allowed him to explore his creativity, develop confidence and discover new strengths. 

Discussions on sustainability further broadened his understanding of how young people can take initiative and contribute towards shaping the future. 

He feels very strongly about getting fellow students to overcome their fears, seize opportunities and recognise that growth begins when we have the courage to take the first step into the unknown. Athan is a student from ITE College Central who participated in the International Student Seminar (ISS) 2026, where he gained opportunities to explore sustainability, media production and cross-cultural collaboration.

Through the programme, he learnt about sustainability through an eco-enzyme workshop, and worked alongside ITE HQ’s Media & Communications team, gaining hands-on experience in videography and video editing.

Beyond acquiring new skills, Athan’s experience enabled him to connect with students from different backgrounds, exchange perspectives and form new friendships. 

His sharing highlights how stepping into an unfamiliar experience can lead to new skills, new connections and unexpected opportunities for growth. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: In Search of Stardust | Jon Larsen | TEDxFredrikstad
recentItems.description: Stardust is falling around us all the time. On rooftops, windowsills and city streets. Jon Larsen tells how an obsessive curiosity about tiny particles led from jazz clubs to microscopes, scientific verification and a new way of finding micrometeorites in urban environments. His story is not only about cosmic dust. It is about attention: how a willingness to look closely at the ordinary can open an unexpected path to discovery, and how science can begin with a simple question that nobody thought worth asking. Jon Larsen is a Norwegian jazz musician, composer, visual artist and citizen scientist. After decades in music, including as a founding figure in Hot Club de Norvège, his curiosity shifted toward tiny particles hidden in everyday dust. Through the Stardust Project he developed methods for distinguishing micrometeorites from human-made particles, contributing to research that helped change how scientists think about collecting modern cosmic dust in populated areas. His journey is a reminder that expertise can begin with sustained curiosity and that discovery sometimes starts by looking closely at what everyone else ignores. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Your skill might be ruining your ability to lead | Jeremy Lutito | TEDxNashville Salon
recentItems.description:
What if the most important thing you bring to a room isn't your talent, expertise, or experience?

After decades as a drummer, songwriter, and music producer, Jeremy Lutito discovered that mastering his craft was only part of what made him valuable. The greater challenge was learning how to influence a creative process without controlling it.

In this TEDxNashville talk, he explores how a quality he once considered a weakness became one of his greatest strengths as a creative leader. 

This talk was presented at TEDxNashville, an independently organized TED event. Jeremy Lutito is a Grammy-nominated producer, songwriter, composer, and multi-instrumentalist based here in Nashville. Known for his versatility and dynamic sound, he has collaborated with artists like Judah & the Lion, Michigander, Little Image, Joy Oladokun, Devon Gilfillian, and more. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What If the Idea You Seek Is Already Around You? | Jiwandeep Singh Ghai (JD Ghai) | TEDxSukhna Lake
recentItems.description:
Where do great ideas come from? And what if the idea you're looking for is already hidden in your everyday experiences?

In this engaging talk, JD Ghai takes us through the unexpected journey behind his venture, one of India's early digital entertainment platforms. What began with a love for humour, an ordinary conversation at a party and a curiosity about the emerging internet eventually became a business that reached millions of people.

Drawing from his 27 years in the digital space, JD Ghai shares how he moved beyond his family's real estate business, took a chance on an unfamiliar industry and built a venture through perseverance, experimentation and an ability to understand changing audience interests.

His message is simple: ideas are all around us. Sometimes, we just need to look at our experiences differently to recognise them. Jiwandeep Singh Ghai (JD Ghai) is a pioneering entrepreneur, digital media leader, and the Founder & CEO of SantaBanta.com, one of India's earliest and most successful entertainment portals. Launched in 1999 as a simple humor website, SantaBanta.com grew under his leadership into a globally recognized digital brand with millions of monthly visitors and a lasting impact on online entertainment.

An MBA from Punjab University, Ghai combines business acumen with a passion for innovation, having expanded the platform across web, mobile, and app ecosystems while continuously adapting to evolving technologies. Beyond entrepreneurship, he is an accomplished sportsman, public speaker, and community leader. A lifelong learner, traveler, and innovator, Ghai continues to inspire others through his journey of resilience, reinvention, and digital entrepreneurship. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: ¡Todos somos primos! | Carlos Santamaría | TEDxPuraVidaSalon
recentItems.description: Costa Rica tuvo pocos pobladores y un antecedente genético muy corto, y por eso es potencia mundial en enfermedades raras. Esta charla explica cómo el estudio de más de 2.400 familias revela que el gen BRCA2 es 8 veces más frecuente aquí que BRCA1. Un llamado a conocer nuestros antecedentes familiares y a tratarnos con empatía y tolerancia. Carlos Santamaría Quesada. Microbiólogo. Máster en Inmunología Clínica UCR. Doctor en Ciencias Médicas (Ph.D.) por la Universidad de Salamanca, España. Premio Nacional de Ciencia “Clodomiro Picado Twight” 2011 por investigación en marcadores moleculares en leucemia. Premio “Doctor Moraza” a la mejor tesis de investigación en Oncología 2011 en Salamanca, España. Jefe del laboratorio de Diagnóstico Molecular, Hospital Nacional de Niños. Docente pregrado y posgrado UCR. Autor de 38 artículos científicos internacionales, conferencista. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
